_meta.purpose: Middle-tier enforcement for JUDGMENT_SOFT patterns — failure modes that recur at 12-40% breadth across the local session corpus (measured 2026-06-21, mega-distill corpus-mode) yet CANNOT be caught by a tool-call hook because they are judgments, not mechanical command shapes. The corpus showed these already have ambient rules that under-enforce under cognitive load (skills-over-rules). This hook injects the SPECIFIC judgment reminder when the relevant work-type is detected in a user prompt — the in-context middle tier between hard hooks (mechanical) and ambient rules (always-on, ignorable).
_meta.design: data-driven: add a pattern = add an entry, no code edit. fail-silent, non-blocking, one reminder per prompt (the highest-breadth match), logged for effectiveness audit.
_meta.h2_validation: the patterns were confirmed NOT to be a rule-anchoring artifact — a blind vocabulary-neutral re-extract (12-session control) independently reproduced 95% of the same clusters.

rules.reminder: PROVE THE INSTRUMENT (recurs in ~40% of large sessions): before publishing any measured/audited number or 'clean/complete/benign' verdict, validate the instrument — confirm the cursor/page is exhausted (one page is never 'complete'), confirm no field was silently dropped or capped, and for perception/consensus questions require >=2 independent instruments reconciled by ID. A number from an unvalidated tool is indistinguishable from a correct one. (verify-effectiveness.md)

OUTCOME, NOT PLUMBING (recurs in ~15% of large sessions; 3 corrections THIS session): 'tests pass / merged / Completed' is plumbing — it is NOT evidence the thing works. Completed != correct (admin-locked skips return exit 0; merged != live). Demonstrate the OUTCOME on real input — run the live path enough times to exercise each branch — before claiming done. (verify-effectiveness.md two-part validation)

STATE THE OPTIMIZATION TARGET FIRST (recurs in ~17% of large sessions): when a recommendation or grade depends on an unstated objective (security vs DR vs cost vs availability; one user vs a team), surface and CONFIRM the objective BEFORE designing or grading — do not silently optimize the most salient one. Multi-mode artifacts need per-mode rubrics. (red-team-rubric-discipline.md / grading-discipline.md)

COUNT IS NOT RISK + ACCOUNT TO 100% (recurs in ~12% of large sessions): never present a raw finding/exposure COUNT as a risk measure — pair every count with its coverage/scan-status ('0 findings' on an INACTIVE resource is a blind spot, not a clean bill), and separate exploitable from best-practice-gap. Before stating any percentage, confirm the categories SUM to 100% of the measured total (no hand-waved remainder). (grading-discipline.md)

GRADE THE ENFORCEMENT MODEL, NOT THE OBSERVED SURFACE (recurs in ~13% of large sessions): before assigning a cloud-security finding's severity, identify the enforcement layer that could neutralize the observed surface (org SCP principal-exception, centralized root mgmt, account-level block-public-access overriding a bucket policy). Granted-scope != exercisable-capability; surface != effective. Read the runtime decision, not the prose/Description. (red-team-rubric-discipline.md / security-critical-search-verification.md)

VERIFY VENDOR BEHAVIOR BEFORE ASSERTING IT (recurs in ~31% of large sessions): a confident 'X behaves like Y' about a third-party system (IAM/policy semantics, API shape, region capability, default behavior) needs a 30-second source check or live probe — NOT training-knowledge confidence — especially when same-corpus evidence is already in front of you. Reconcile against any retrieved doc/KB before stating it. (verify-before-assuming.md)

CROSS EVERY SEAM TO THE REAL SINK (recurs THIS session 4x: #528 investigate-query, #690 health date_diff, #693 brief-render, + the 'is it deployed?' loop): merged != applied != resource-updated != code-correct != RUNS-on-real-data. 'Green CI / merged / IAM-verified / unit-test-green' is NOT deployed — a unit test that STUBS the sink never crosses the seam that breaks (the bug lives in the seam: query-vs-real-schema, producer-vs-consumer, esp. CROSS-REPO mcp-servers<->mcp-infra). Verify with ONE real run that crosses every seam to the real sink (real Athena query against real data / real Lambda invoke / the deployed artifact's actual code / the consumer actually renders the producer's output), and for a deployed resource check the resource's own state (LastModified advanced, ResolvedImageUri == the commit), never the workflow's green check. (verify-effectiveness.md multi_seam invariant)
